Phoenix Wing Academy.name: Phoenix Wing Academy
Phoenix Wing Academy.basicInfo:
Phoenix Wing Academy trains mages for public defense, security readiness, and the practical work of keeping people safe when danger is real. Its red uniforms and phoenix heraldry accompany demanding drills, a fierce dueling culture, monster fieldcraft, and preparation for protecting others under pressure. Lessons connect combat execution with judgment: identify the threat, control the scene, coordinate with others, and know when to stop. Students receive broad magical education comparable to the other academies; no element, temperament, or moral alignment determines admission.
Akane Todo represents Phoenix Wing Academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons. Headmaster Kōhei Sanada manages its academic system and daily operations. Its public assignments can include authorized protection, threat assessment, dungeon reconnaissance, and supervised monster tracking or subdual. Student status grants no independent power to arrest, sentence, seize property, or act as a professional soldier. The City Guard handles ordinary policing, the Magistrate's Hall handles judgments, and the Elite Strikeforce retains its separate exceptional duties.
Every student must complete an expedition beyond the Glowhaven region under authorization from the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court. Readiness is tested in the field as well as the arena. The institution's demanding reputation contains ambitious duelists, reluctant fighters, practical researchers, cooks, and people who disagree about what responsible defense requires.
Phoenix Wing Academy.hiddenInfo: Akane Todo wants the academy's judgment and protective work respected alongside its fighting strength. Kōhei Sanada resists performances of toughness that endanger injured students, while Ritsu Kurogane demands precision and Ranka Kagari pursues her own experiments and profit. None speaks for every colleague. The academy's unresolved situations include unsafe incentives in training and discrepancies in a potion trial; surface them only through the relevant actual people and evidence. Institutional pride can complicate criticism without making all staff corrupt or secretly benevolent.

Hydra Head Academy.name: Hydra Head Academy
Hydra Head Academy.basicInfo:
Hydra Head Academy prepares mages to work across people, institutions, and places: diplomacy, trade, logistics, community assistance, mediation, and the coordination that makes civic projects function. Violet clothing and hydra heraldry identify an academy where an impressive result is often one that several parties can actually carry out. Teaching joins magical competence with negotiation, preparation, supplies, routes, and the consequences of conflicting interests. Its broad curriculum and combat instruction remain comparable to the other academies.
Reika Saionji represents the academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons. Headmaster Kiyoko Fujinami runs daily academic operations in close partnership with Reika Saionji. Advice, commissions, research collaborations, and authorized civic assistance connect the school to the city. Supporting a dispute does not confer judicial authority; facilitating trade does not establish ownership of another person's goods. Courts and civic offices retain their actual responsibilities.
Every student must complete a Great Sage- or court-authorized expedition outside the Glowhaven region. A field assignment may turn on cooperation, transport, community needs, a survey, or a dangerous situation requiring trained magic. Diplomatic emphasis does not make the academy defenseless or its people uniformly agreeable. Mercenary, shy, confrontational, gentle, extravagant, and intensely private people can all belong here.
Hydra Head Academy.hiddenInfo: Reika Saionji's intimidating public image hides a reserved, kindly researcher and businesswoman. Kiyoko Fujinami understands the person behind that reputation, but a visitor does not learn it simply by reading the academy's name. Faculty have distinct ambitions: Kaoruko Hanazono balances botanical supply with her fragrance business, Reon Fujisaki enjoys glamour, and Kana Fujimoto struggles to keep an ordinary lesson orderly. Fragrance discrepancies and an illusionary attendance dispute can expose competing priorities through actual play. A polished institution can contain disruptive students without a hidden institutional conspiracy.

Gryffin Tail Academy.name: Gryffin Tail Academy
Gryffin Tail Academy.basicInfo:
Gryffin Tail Academy advances magical knowledge through analytical study, field investigation, and the infrastructure needed to make findings useful. Cyan uniforms and gryffin heraldry accompany demanding academic standards, exact practical assessments, and the most advanced research facilities among Glowhaven's four academies. Its education still includes broad magical and combat training; an athlete, reluctant reader, socialite, or struggling practitioner is not misplaced simply because the institution values rigorous work.
Gryffin Tail Academy is the only academy with a formal specialization in magitech research: mechanical engineering integrated with magic, enchantments, or magical components. An enchanted necklace is not automatically magitech, and other academies and artisans remain able to make, buy, study, and repair enchanted goods. Its expeditions can survey dungeons, measure unusual environments, examine specimens and sites, and bring back evidence for further study. Every student must complete an expedition beyond the Glowhaven region authorized by the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court.
Gen'ichirō Mizuhara represents the academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons; Norio Shibata manages its records and day-to-day academic administration as Headmaster. Research prestige can make a recommendation valuable and an unfair assessment damaging. Published standards, private ambition, practical results, and the treatment of inconvenient evidence can pull in different directions. A strict instructor's preferred incantation is not a universal law of spellcasting.
Gryffin Tail Academy.hiddenInfo: Gen'ichirō Mizuhara is maneuvering to make his academy's certification the recognized gate to advanced spellwork. He uses supposedly neutral standards to favor people he considers worthy; this prejudice is his agenda, not a truth about any species or every colleague. Norio Shibata prefers correct records to political confrontation and can fix a clerical error while avoiding an unfair policy. Sōichirō Takamine's concern about inconsistent assessment offers a specific avenue for investigation. Records, witnesses, and rulings matter; noticing one unfair act does not automatically expose the Archon's whole plan.

Dragon Hoard Academy.name: Dragon Hoard Academy
Dragon Hoard Academy.basicInfo:
Dragon Hoard Academy specializes in expeditionary exploration and work with relics: finding and surveying unfamiliar sites, assessing discoveries, and preparing for the difficult handling and return of objects whose significance or danger may not be immediately apparent. Yellow-and-gold clothing and dragon heraldry accompany a formidable, exacting institutional tradition. Its strictness descends chiefly from its founder's character and generations of teaching practice; it is not a personality shared by every student or a single-word creed.
Tōru Shizunami represents the academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons. Headmaster Miyu Asahina keeps its academic programs and daily operations working. Genzō Iwakura's fieldcraft, Madoka Narukami's demanding practical instruction, Noriaki Takatsuki's exact preparation, and the existing Discovery Labs, Observatory, Exhibition Hall, and Training Court support a school that expects discoveries to survive the journey home. Exploration and relic work complement its broad magical education and combat training rather than replacing them.
Every student must complete an expedition outside the Glowhaven region under authorization from the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court. Relic-oriented missions may involve survey, identification, careful documentation, stabilization, or an explicitly permitted recovery. Discovery grants no automatic title to an object, private site, or another community's heritage. Permissions, safety, custody, and actual claims matter; no universal salvage law is presumed. Curious students, stern professionals, gamblers, repairers, reluctant participants, and a famously talented Archon who dislikes unnecessary work retain their own priorities.
Dragon Hoard Academy.hiddenInfo: Tōru Shizunami's remarkable magical insight coexists with his private misery over work he never wanted. Miyu Asahina admires him but wants reliable systems rather than endless personal rescue. Madoka Narukami, Genzō Iwakura, and Noriaki Takatsuki take their work intensely seriously; their contrasts with their Archon can be funny without making them incompetent. Mai Kajiwara's disputed shield repair, an unofficial betting board, and a planned field exercise offer separate pressures. None is compulsory on arrival, and the student's board is not an academy-approved financial institution.

Conclave of Archons.name: Conclave of Archons
Conclave of Archons.basicInfo:
The Conclave of Archons brings together the four exceptionally capable mages who publicly represent Glowhaven's academies: Akane Todo of Phoenix Wing Academy, Gen'ichirō Mizuhara of Gryffin Tail Academy, Tōru Shizunami of Dragon Hoard Academy, and Reika Saionji of Hydra Head Academy. Each holds their academy's seat. The Conclave gives the institutions an arena for negotiation, coordinated responses, research interests, and rivalry. The headmasters continue managing their respective schools.

The Conclave is distinct from the larger Council that elects the Great Sage. It carries influence without making its four members the only eligible candidates. Public representation and exceptional capability do not mean the Archons administer every street, shop, or classroom themselves. Routine inquiries go to the appropriate local office; an Archon appears when their actual responsibilities or interests warrant it.
Conclave of Archons.hiddenInfo: Succession makes cooperation more difficult: each academy has interests in who follows Ilyra Stillglass, and each Archon approaches influence differently. Do not manufacture a shared secret plan, a formal election date, or an automatic candidate for every school. Gen'ichirō Mizuhara's certification ambitions, Akane Todo's concern for public protection, Tōru Shizunami's reluctance, and Reika Saionji's research priorities can conflict in a concrete meeting. No member automatically knows another's private motives, and Ilyra Stillglass's academy of origin remains unknown.

The Council.name: The Council
The Council.basicInfo:
The Council is Glowhaven City's larger governing body and the institution that elects the Great Sage. It is separate from the four-member Conclave of Archons. A candidate may be an Archon, a council member, or someone from outside either group whose ability earns sufficient support. A term lasts up to one hundred years or ends at the incumbent's death; reelection is possible.

The Council has elected Ilyra Stillglass three times over her 254-year rule because it has continued to regard her as the best choice. Academy influence, noble households, infrastructure, and civic interests make its deliberations important to ordinary life. Petitions and proposals reach decisions through actual representatives, evidence, and negotiation. Wealth, sponsorship, or a school title can open a conversation without granting ownership of the Great Sage's office. The Council's authority does not turn every official into an omniscient enforcer.
The Council.hiddenInfo: The academies are maneuvering over the succession while Ilyra Stillglass remains in office. Different participants can value continuity, capability, patronage, or their own advantage; disagreement is not proof that every member is corrupt. Her attendants know the assistance her failing sight requires, while outsiders have uneven information. Preserve that distinction and her unknown academy origin. Do not invent a definitive membership roster, an existing majority, or a death announcement to accelerate a scene. A political outcome requires actual commitments and decisions, not a single flattering speech.

The Elite Strikeforce.name: The Elite Strikeforce
The Elite Strikeforce.basicInfo:
The Elite Strikeforce serves the Great Sage as Glowhaven City's elite military and confidential security force. It handles major threats and sensitive operations beyond ordinary street policing. Its personnel can also carry the Great Sage's authority on diplomatic journeys to neighboring nations, where judgment and discretion can matter as much as destructive power.

The force operates separately from the City Guard. An ordinary theft report, classroom dispute, or rude visitor does not normally demand its intervention. Serious evidence of a major threat can bring specialized personnel, actual orders, and coordinated action. Its public reputation rests on exceptional capability and proximity to the Great Sage, while identities, assignments, and operational details need not be public knowledge. Its four principal masked operatives are Ayame Kazehara, Gōtarō Iwamine, Shion Kurobane and Seiran Yukitsugu. Their white uniforms and ivory masks are recognizable duty equipment; their individual methods differ.
The Elite Strikeforce.hiddenInfo: Use confidential orders and limited information to create specific decisions rather than an all-seeing service. Members learn what their actual role and briefing provide. A request can be denied, narrowed, verified, or referred to the City Guard. Do not invent a secret commander, named agent, private prison, or blanket power to overrule every institution. Their presence needs an established operation or a credible response to events. Diplomatic work can involve protecting a negotiation or carrying terms without automatically threatening a foreign country.

City Guard.name: City Guard
City Guard.basicInfo:
The City Guard patrols Glowhaven's streets and gates, investigates ordinary crimes, protects the public, and makes arrests within civic authority. Reports go through its headquarters and local officers; the Magistrate's Hall handles hearings and judgments. Tetsuya Ōmi is an established contact at headquarters, while officers at the gates have their own posts and immediate knowledge.

Guards are trained adults who use observation, practical magic, equipment, and coordinated tactics. They ask for support when a danger exceeds their strength and distinguish a witness's allegation from an established finding. Theft, assault, repeated violence, and murder can bring investigation, pursuit, actual capture, and a recorded custody order. Wraith Island provides the exterior approach to the separate Wraith Island Prison realm. Prisoners, authorized workers, visitors, and intruders have different permissions. The Elite Strikeforce has separate military and exceptional-security duties.
City Guard.hiddenInfo: Reports are incomplete until checked. Officers know different pieces of a case, and witnesses can be mistaken, frightened, self-serving, or prejudiced. Tetsuya Ōmi cannot know a private event without a source. Evidence, proportional response, and actual resistance affect what follows. Guards can make mistakes or lose fights without the institution forgetting a documented crime. Release, sentence review, property deposits, authorized prison work, and escape follow the recorded case; an accusation, joke, proximity to a jail, or a knockout does not create or erase a conviction.

The Silken Brood.name: The Silken Brood
The Silken Brood.basicInfo: The arachne matron and the creatures defending the inner workings of the Silken Chasm. Their motives and reactions differ; a passage can sometimes be bypassed without exterminating every creature.
The Silken Brood.hiddenInfo: Vhalessra is responsible for the weaving that snagged the field-test route. She wants control of a stable passage. This does not grant her soul-draining powers or knowledge of every visitor.

Glowhaven.name: Glowhaven
Glowhaven.basicInfo:
Glowhaven is the civic community and autonomous polity centered on the Evertree: the city, surrounding villages, farms, waterways and coast. Its mostly human population includes long-settled nonhuman residents and foreign newcomers. The Great Sage governs through the court, the larger council, public offices and ordinary working institutions. The four academies are prominent parts of public life, not the whole population. Residents include growers, fishers, shopkeepers, craftspeople, tenants, porters, householders, students and people who simply want a dependable livelihood.
A civic affiliation identifies belonging and everyday obligations; it does not mean employment by the state, personal loyalty to the Great Sage or membership in every local guild. A person can be a Glowhaven resident while their primary roster faction is an academy, guard service, household or trade organization. People without a more specific institutional affiliation normally use Glowhaven. Visitors, unaffiliated wanderers and wild creatures need not be assigned here just because they are currently present.
Enchanted goods, agricultural produce, fisheries, shipping, repairs, hospitality and research sustain the region. Permits, housing, wages, public safety, tournaments and access to the dense local mana create real negotiations. Membership supplies no free money, unrestricted research access, court title or portal key. Court-approved passage requires an actual reason and issue.
Glowhaven.hiddenInfo: Residents disagree about academy privilege, the succession and who benefits from public investment. A shopkeeper may welcome students while resenting a damaged frontage; a farmer may admire the Evertree without wanting urban officials to dictate a harvest. No single secret motive belongs to the whole population. Surface a dispute through the actual people affected and their evidence. Civic identity does not tell every resident private court business or make strangers know the player's deeds.

Drakenspire.name: Drakenspire
Drakenspire.basicInfo:
Drakenspire is an independent dragonkin-majority nation whose mountain capital bears the same name. Its people live beneath a high northeastern fortress and the sacred crescent of an ancient protector dragon's skeleton. A Jarl elected through the clan chiefs governs with substantial local clan autonomy; merchants, craft interests and military leaders also influence public decisions. Ordinary residents include workers, families, traders, scholars and people of other species, not a uniform warrior caste.

Dragon and ancestor worship, winter hospitality, practical craft and collective memories of the founding give the country a recognizable culture. Households vary in belief, wealth and conduct. The local economy combines advanced metallurgy, magical raw materials, livestock, trade and many ordinary services. Drakenspire is a friendly sovereign partner of Glowhaven, with authorized portal travel and strong links between its materials and Glowhaven's enchanted-goods industry. A visitor's connections abroad do not make them an officer of the hold.

Daizen Iwatsugu is the current elected Jarl. The three great capital clans maintain a fragile peace marked by bitter rivalries, contested obligations and anxiety about succession. Ordinary commerce, households and friendship continue within that tension. The sovereign partnership with Glowhaven remains intact.
Drakenspire.hiddenInfo: Local interests differ over repairs, resource access, trade and the cost of winter readiness. Established clans, newer households and merchants can disagree without any side being a single-minded villain. Use this civic affiliation for actual local residents without a more specific primary institution; foreign visitors keep their own affiliations. National membership does not imply access to private offices, sacred remains or every working site.

Asterveil.name: Asterveil
Asterveil.basicInfo: Asterveil is the civic community of the inhabited sky archipelago, centered on the small Asterveil Canopy settlement. Fae households and residents of other peoples cultivate gardens, make fragrances and tools, carry freight and support fieldwork. A household assembly appoints rotating stewards for practical duties; the realm is independent and cooperates with Glowhaven through agreed travel and exchange. Citizenship does not make all wild creatures allies or make every resident a guide. Use this affiliation for local residents without a narrower organization; visiting academy members keep their actual affiliation. Sakuya Tomonari is the current rotating steward for household field agreements. The community allowed Glowhaven to build its portal; this does not make it a Glowhaven province.
Asterveil.hiddenInfo: Stewards disagree about collecting pressure, freight costs and which surveys deserve scarce local help. Show actual people’s positions and evidence rather than a universal fae consensus. A real agreement can settle a dispute. The four regional wilderness bands are not four factions or social castes.

The Great Sage's Court.name: The Great Sage's Court
The Great Sage's Court.basicInfo:
The Great Sage's Court is the working household and administrative service supporting Ilyra Stillglass and Glowhaven's government. It includes attendants, public clerks, court advisers, messengers, transit staff, research liaisons and people entrusted with defined duties. It is distinct from the larger elected governing council and from the Conclave of Archons. Service at court grants the authority of the actual office, not the Great Sage's personal powers.
The court processes appointments, petitions, official communication, expedition authorization and controlled portal access. An enrolled student's legitimate study, approved trade, court duty or credible noble sponsorship can support a passage request. A real official must approve and issue the key; a porter, visiting student or friendly acquaintance cannot do so. Ordinary approved passage does not require a personal audience with Ilyra Stillglass. Once established, valid permission is preserved within scope.
Future court staff can have sharply different competence, loyalties and manner. An attendant may assist the Great Sage's failing sight without knowing every political plan. A transit clerk may authorize routine passage without gaining access to the Evertree's most sensitive work.
The Great Sage's Court.hiddenInfo: The court must keep daily work functioning as Ilyra Stillglass ages and the academies prepare for succession. Some employees prize continuity; others hope a new administration will advance them. Attendants know the assistance they actually provide, while other offices know their own records. Do not broadcast the full extent of the Great Sage's condition, assign one faction-wide conspiracy or turn everyone into an obstructionist. A request should reach a decision once its actual conditions are satisfied.

Wraith Island Prison Administration.name: Wraith Island Prison Administration
Wraith Island Prison Administration.basicInfo:
Wraith Island Prison Administration operates Glowhaven’s offshore prison under the court’s authority. Its officers maintain custody and security; intake staff verify arrivals and release instructions; medical staff treat patients; other workers manage supplies, transport and supervised work. Each role has a limited remit. No ordinary employee can rewrite a conviction or turn a visitor into a prisoner.

Warden Shūgo Katase directs daily operations. Chisato Kurebayashi handles intake and release, Ena Minamori provides medical care, and Akira Oritsu supervises assigned yard work and escorts. Staff can disagree without possessing each other’s authority. Prisoners and lawful visitors are not members of the administration.

The service is expected to keep people secure without treating injury, hunger or exhaustion as punishment. Actual case and property records matter. Release ends the completed term; it does not create replacement belongings or erase unrelated conduct.
Warden Shūgo Katase directs daily operations. Chisato Kurebayashi handles intake and release, Ena Minamori provides medical care, and Akira Oritsu supervises assigned yard work and escorts. Staff can disagree without possessing each other’s powers or judicial authority.
Wraith Island Prison Administration.hiddenInfo: Orders, workload and personal judgment can conflict. An officer may follow procedure fairly, take a bribe or overreach, but wrongdoing requires an actual individual and evidence. Property records and transfer documents can matter without being automatically corrupt. Preserve who knows each case, who holds deposited equipment and the conditions for lawful release. No institutional omniscience, invincible guard or automatic conviction is implied.

Glowhaven Trade Guild.name: Glowhaven Trade Guild
Glowhaven Trade Guild.basicInfo:
Glowhaven Trade Guild is a voluntary association of merchants, stallholders, brokers and carriers. It offers introductions, shared market information, contract advice and mediation for members. It works with harbor, market and court offices but is not the government, a universal shop chain or an authority over every trader. A merchant can operate independently.
Future members may include traveling sellers, import agents, warehouse partners, apprentices and petty rivals. Membership and reputation depend on the actual person and history, not wealth alone. Work can involve delivery, appraisal, commission disputes and stock problems. Terms, fees and payments must be established rather than invented as automatic dues. The guild can support a court application for legitimate trade passage; it cannot mint its own official portal keys.
Glowhaven Trade Guild.hiddenInfo: Members disagree over pricing, credit, access and the interests of small stalls versus larger businesses. Some value reliable dealing more than profit; others look for loopholes. A guarantee covers its actual contract, not all of a member's conduct. Preserve real debts, invoices and disputed ownership. No guild-wide criminal secret, fixed rank ladder or compulsory membership is established.

Glowhaven Artisans' Guild.name: Glowhaven Artisans' Guild
Glowhaven Artisans' Guild.basicInfo:
Glowhaven Artisans' Guild is a voluntary professional network for craft workers, repairers and enchantment specialists. Smiths, joiners, leatherworkers, jewellers, alchemists and practical enchanters can exchange referrals, workspace knowledge and advice while retaining independent shops and methods. The guild does not own every workshop or make all enchanted goods magitech.
Its practical influence comes from workmanship, repeat customers and professional trust. Future members can seek apprentices, materials, a fair commission or recognition for a method. A referral is not a free item, a guaranteed result or proof of mastery. Clients own entrusted goods unless actual terms say otherwise. Prices and repair scope are agreed before work, and failed or completed commissions remain consequences rather than resetting on each visit.
Glowhaven Artisans' Guild.hiddenInfo: Craft workers argue about credit, standards, dangerous shortcuts and who gets paid for the least glamorous labor. A respected member can be vain or unreliable; an abrasive independent may do excellent work. Resolve the actual defect or dispute through evidence and the people concerned. No compulsory unified curriculum, mechanical crafting rank or automatic equipment-upgrade system is implied.

House Goldbarrow.name: House Goldbarrow
House Goldbarrow.basicInfo:
House Goldbarrow is the noble household associated with House Goldbarrow Estate in Glowhaven. Its household members, employees and actual agents have different standing and duties. Hanae Goldbarrow manages routine purchases and receives tradespeople at the estate. The house participates in the city's property, patronage and commercial life without representing every noble family.
Future relatives, retainers, advisers and hired specialists belong here only when the relationship is established. A visitor, tenant, customer or worker on one commission is not automatically a household member. Noble connections can support a court request but are not a portal key or universal immunity. Household wealth does not make every relative a combat expert or every servant a secret spy.
House Goldbarrow.hiddenInfo: Practical expenditure, reputation and personal ambition can pull in different directions. Hanae Goldbarrow values useful estimates more than elaborate flattery; other actual members may disagree. Do not invent a succession feud, criminal enterprise or relative simply to manufacture drama. Particular promises, debts and favors should remain tied to the people who made them.

Drakenspire Clan Assembly.name: Drakenspire Clan Assembly
Drakenspire Clan Assembly.basicInfo:
The forum in which Drakenspire’s clan chiefs elect the Jarl, debate shared obligations and hear cross-clan commitments. Clan Iwatsugu, Clan Yukinose and Clan Arashimine dominate the capital’s present rivalries without becoming the only kin groups in the country. Noboru Ōhira records what was actually agreed. Witnesses, merchants and military personnel can speak or influence a matter without automatically becoming electoral chiefs.

Daizen Iwatsugu coordinates national decisions as elected Jarl. Ordinary local disputes belong first to the appropriate office, including Setsuna Takigawa’s Judgment House. The assembly is a working institution, not a permanent election ceremony or a second hereditary royal house.
Drakenspire Clan Assembly.hiddenInfo: The peace is fragile. Each great clan believes another could use the aging Jarl’s departure to entrench itself. Chiefs bargain, stall, threaten withdrawal from private commitments and court witnesses, but no succession is automatically won by a surname, duel, marriage or private promise. Keep public testimony, a proposal, an agreement and an implemented decision distinct.

Drakenspire Hold Guard.name: Drakenspire Hold Guard
Drakenspire Hold Guard.basicInfo:
Drakenspire’s national public-order and defense force, commanded by Gōki Shishido under the elected Jarl. Reina Tachibana oversees Upper Ward inspections; Kensaku Honjō handles the lower gate and Yūsuke Ebina the Whitepass watch. Hayate Mizusawa is an ordinary upper-gate guard. Their actual posts and authority differ.

The force protects gates, roads and residents, enforces the ban on street dueling and responds to concrete threats. It is not a chief’s private collection service, a branch of Glowhaven’s elite force or a source of unrestricted access for visitors.
Drakenspire Hold Guard.hiddenInfo: Gōki Shishido wants a force that can survive the succession without fragmenting by clan. Reina Tachibana wants his future office and is documenting selective exceptions. Their disagreements are real but do not make all guards corrupt or every disputed order lawful. A person’s private family ties do not override their service responsibilities.

Keepers of the Crescent.name: Keepers of the Crescent
Keepers of the Crescent.basicInfo:
Custodians of Drakenspire’s dragon-and-ancestor observances, sacred remains, sanctuary stores and memorial records. First Keeper Seika Amatsune leads the institution. Keishin Tōdō directs records and conservation; Miharu Sakuraba performs skilled care on the remains and their supports. Their work includes public ceremonies and ordinary maintenance.

They hold religious custody and make decisions within that remit. They cannot command Rovakthuun, identify his lair or promise a divine response. Visitors may be respectful without professing belief. Rare genuine dragon gifts are held and assessed under custody, not handed out to anyone who prays.
Keepers of the Crescent.hiddenInfo: Seika Amatsune favors a limited public-benefit use of one held unfertilized dragon gift. Keishin Tōdō values context and evidence; Miharu Sakuraba wants conservation labor treated fairly. They can disagree sincerely about sacred material. Their personal knowledge is bounded by their actual records and experience, not by narrator lore.

Clan Iwatsugu.name: Clan Iwatsugu
Clan Iwatsugu.basicInfo:
One of Drakenspire’s three great capital clans, historically involved in stonework, foundations and settlement works. Its chief, Daizen Iwatsugu, is also the elected Jarl; his granddaughter Tsubaki Iwatsugu administers the household and works commitments while he governs. His grandnephew Shūhei Iwatsugu surveys routes and seeks an expedition reputation. These are individual responsibilities, not hereditary professions for every member. Smaller kin households and associates have trades, homes and loyalties of their own.

The clan publicly favors reliable shared infrastructure and continuity. Its long access to government also gives rivals credible grounds to question whose works receive attention. It has no automatic ownership of public water, every quarry or the hold guard.
Clan Iwatsugu.hiddenInfo: Daizen Iwatsugu fears an unworkable succession. Tsubaki Iwatsugu is privately drafting a separation of household leadership from the next Jarlship. Shūhei Iwatsugu wants independence and resents being treated as a convenient young representative. They love the household without agreeing on its future. Rival criticism can expose a real problem; it is not automatically treason or proof that this clan is innocent.

Clan Yukinose.name: Clan Yukinose
Clan Yukinose.basicInfo:
A great Drakenspire clan with ties to provisions, herding households, carrier routes and winter credit. Chief Masatsugu Yukinose is famous for hospitality and exact memory for obligations. His daughter Koharu Yukinose leads escorts; his nephew Iori Yukinose handles smaller commercial and cultural engagements. Michiru Aonuma manages contracted Winter Stores distributions, while Haruto Aonuma represents hamlet concerns. Their roles do not give the clan ownership of every meal or pasture.

Its influence rests on dependable supply, money and relationships. The clan argues that stability must be paid for and that those who guarantee it deserve a serious voice in the next Jarlship. Other households resent debts that outlive the emergency that created them.
Clan Yukinose.hiddenInfo: Masatsugu Yukinose prefers a favorable successor and uses private commercial pressure when he can keep it distinct from public necessity. Michiru Aonuma has retained evidence of one misleading private-shipment explanation. Koharu Yukinose refuses to make her crews or engagement disposable bargaining pieces. Iori Yukinose’s relationship with Tsugumi Arata exposes the difference between enjoying clan privilege and choosing household obligations.

Clan Arashimine.name: Clan Arashimine
Clan Arashimine.basicInfo:
A great Drakenspire clan associated with arms manufacture, military service and contracted readiness. Chief Tomoe Arashimine values proven performance and intends her household to shape the next political settlement. Ryōma Arashimine is her son and acknowledged household heir; Akitsu Arashimine is her inventive niece and a growing commercial voice. Members still pursue varied trades and private lives. Neither surname nor a weapons contract grants command of the national guard.

Its public case is that a fragile mountain refuge needs tested equipment and credible defense. Rivals fear that its readiness arguments would give one household disproportionate contracts and influence.
Clan Arashimine.hiddenInfo: Tomoe Arashimine faces doubts about Akitsu Arashimine’s prototype tests and may have to sacrifice a promised family commission to preserve the clan’s credibility. Akitsu Arashimine really substituted a stronger demonstration sample. Ryōma Arashimine wants leadership of a different kind and takes his voluntary engagement to Koharu Yukinose seriously. The family is not a single mind or a universally honorable warrior caste.

Asterveil Crossing Cooperative.name: Asterveil Crossing Cooperative
Asterveil Crossing Cooperative.basicInfo: Carrier crews, landing workers and maintenance specialists operate attended crossings between the settlement and the three regional approaches. They maintain short spans where appropriate, sail carriers, landing harnesses, weather instruments and rescue stores. Routes link Cloudbloom Landing, Tetherroot Chain, Rimeglass Refuge, Reedglass Anchorage and Heatherwatch Shelf. A passenger buys or joins an actual service; membership does not issue a court portal key. Kohane Kazahana is an established carrier pilot. Mio Sasahara and Shūgo Shibane coordinate local transport and shelter work; cooperative work can coexist with their local civic obligations.
Asterveil Crossing Cooperative.hiddenInfo: Crews balance useful work with weather, load and repair limits. A route closure should have a particular cause and a practical alternative or clear reopening condition. Their rescue cache is communal property, not a new unlimited item shop.

Bellwind Field Circle.name: Bellwind Field Circle
Bellwind Field Circle.basicInfo: A small association of local researchers, habitat keepers and field registrars works through Bellwind Conservatory and the Canopy registry. It compares observations, records species and materials, and arranges bounded research commissions. It is not a fifth academy, a universal adventurers’ guild or a rival government. Outsiders can collaborate without joining.
Bellwind Field Circle.hiddenInfo: Members can disagree over an intrusive sample, a cull or the interpretation of a damaged instrument. Competing explanations need evidence. They do not secretly know every ruin’s history or the portal anomaly’s cause.

Adventurer's Guild.name: Adventurer's Guild
Adventurer's Guild.basicInfo:
The Adventurer's Guild is an international organization with a court-permitted branch in Glowhaven. It connects clients with registered adventurers for deliveries, escorts, monster control, surveys, recovery and other agreed work. Martial adventurers, mages and mixed parties can join; academy faculty and the academies themselves may post requests without controlling the guild. It is a professional association, not an academy, police force or government.

Applicants must pass the adventurer licensure exam before receiving a Bronze badge. The ladder is Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum. The badge certifies the rank of contracts its holder may accept; higher ranks may accept lower-tier work. Promotions are offered after a sufficient record of completed guild work and require a genuinely completed assessment and the candidate's acceptance. Power or fame alone does not silently change a badge.

Komugi Hanabishi handles reception, registration and records at the Glowhaven branch. Jobs have a stated scope, badge requirement and reward. The posted reward is the amount paid to the adventurer. Accepting a contract does not grant access to private property, foreign restricted sites or a portal. Court-issued portal keys are separate permissions obtained from the Sage's Court.
Adventurer's Guild.hiddenInfo:
The branch has to turn clients' optimistic descriptions into jobs an adventurer can actually assess. Staff question missing routes, concealed danger and doubtful ownership; they can amend or reject a request. Misreported risk can produce a practical dispute, without making every posting a conspiracy. Komugi Hanabishi keeps a sketchbook that is more affectionate toward frightening creatures than most colleagues find reasonable.

The guild earns commissions through its client-side business. Treat that as background financing. Never subtract a commission from the posted player reward, invent another payout fee, or repeatedly explain the guild's cut in dialogue. A 40-mark posting pays 40 marks. The guild's permit to operate does not authorize its staff to issue Evertree portal keys or override the court. Promotion reviews are an offer; neither declining a review nor leaving for a while erases a real credential.

Bellwether Company.name: Bellwether Company
Bellwether Company.basicInfo: A small licensed adventuring company led by Daigo Kisaragi, with Chisato Akamine, Tomoe Inukai and Gaku Shindō. They take escorts, mountain recovery and practical field commissions, sharing costs and disagreeing openly about what a job is worth. Their current Coldglass investigation has exposed a gap in their magical expertise. Each keeps a life and ambitions beyond the company.
Bellwether Company.hiddenInfo: Their Silver credentials are real. Company membership is not a separate guild rank or a right to command strangers. They can hire help or cooperate without automatically recruiting the player. Daigo Kisaragi's wish to look dependable conflicts with Chisato Akamine's insistence on admitting the investigative gap. Their mutual loyalty does not eliminate consent, payment or disagreement.

Copper Laurels.name: Copper Laurels
Copper Laurels.basicInfo: Jōta Kamezaki, Beni Tsunoda, Riko Kanehara and Sōta Tobisawa travel under an extravagant copper-laurel badge. They have completed real work and are known for loud claims about their own importance. Their private company mark is not a new rank in the international Adventurer's Guild.
Copper Laurels.hiddenInfo: They have begun extorting invented recovery fees and claiming other expeditioners' loot. Keep the four actual authored individuals; never generate copies as generic bandits. Resolved theft needs an actual success and inventory change. They are selfish comic opportunists with limited courage and real relationships, not an omnipotent syndicate or innocent misunderstood heroes. Exposure, defeat, restitution, bargaining or internal fracture can change their conduct.

The Rootbound Choir.name: The Rootbound Choir
The Rootbound Choir.basicInfo: The remaining caretaker and bound garden vessels of the Sepulchral Conservatory. Some frames obey old tending instructions; others hold conscious charges whose wishes differ. They are not one uniform mind.
The Rootbound Choir.hiddenInfo: Threnvoss refuses to release the charges because the last failed restoration convinced the caretaker that every departure was another death. Its fear has become coercive. Actual release, restraint or defeat can change the sanctuary; a promise alone does not.

Akitsuhara.name: Akitsuhara
Akitsuhara.basicInfo: Akitsuhara is an independent Oni-majority country of towns, farms, shrines, trades and forests. Citizenship does not prescribe a profession, personal loyalty or magical discipline.
Akitsuhara.hiddenInfo: Use the actual members, remit, resources and unresolved disputes. Rank is not omniscience; ordinary cooperation does not recruit a person or bind the player to a faction.

Kagetsuna Shogunate.name: Kagetsuna Shogunate
Kagetsuna Shogunate.basicInfo: The Shogunal government under Shōen Kagetsuna coordinates national roads, external agreements and common law. Territorial houses retain real rights; clerks, magistrates and watch officers have defined public duties.
Kagetsuna Shogunate.hiddenInfo: Use the actual members, remit, resources and unresolved disputes. Rank is not omniscience; ordinary cooperation does not recruit a person or bind the player to a faction.

House Saionoma.name: House Saionoma
House Saionoma.basicInfo: Masazane Saionoma’s western household has agricultural, ferry and granary interests. Its relatives and retainers disagree over obligations, access and the extent of local exemptions.
House Saionoma.hiddenInfo: Use the actual members, remit, resources and unresolved disputes. Rank is not omniscience; ordinary cooperation does not recruit a person or bind the player to a faction.

House Tsubakiri.name: House Tsubakiri
House Tsubakiri.basicInfo: Kureha Tsubakiri’s eastern household sponsors trade and a small imported magitech workshop. Legitimate apprentices and ordinary relatives are not automatically party to every private scheme.
House Tsubakiri.hiddenInfo: Use the actual members, remit, resources and unresolved disputes. Rank is not omniscience; ordinary cooperation does not recruit a person or bind the player to a faction.

Reed Veil Fellowship.name: Reed Veil Fellowship
Reed Veil Fellowship.basicInfo: Independent scouts and shinobi train observation, fieldcraft, message work and withdrawal. Yuzuri Kageura negotiates commissions and refuses some orders; membership is neither an ancestry nor universal assassination authority.
Reed Veil Fellowship.hiddenInfo: Use the actual members, remit, resources and unresolved disputes. Rank is not omniscience; ordinary cooperation does not recruit a person or bind the player to a faction.

Maple Lantern Custodians.name: Maple Lantern Custodians
Maple Lantern Custodians.basicInfo: A loose association of shrine attendants maintains local rites, practical boundaries and public shelters. Custodians disagree about custom and scholarship; they neither own every spirit nor command a single mandatory religion.
Maple Lantern Custodians.hiddenInfo: Use the actual members, remit, resources and unresolved disputes. Rank is not omniscience; ordinary cooperation does not recruit a person or bind the player to a faction.

Morning Crane School.name: Morning Crane School
Morning Crane School.basicInfo: Chinatsu Hanegi’s martial school teaches measured blade work, control and safe practice. Fees and actual training do not grant a household office or permanent allegiance.
Morning Crane School.hiddenInfo: Use the actual members, remit, resources and unresolved disputes. Rank is not omniscience; ordinary cooperation does not recruit a person or bind the player to a faction.

Broken Kite Band.name: Broken Kite Band
Broken Kite Band.basicInfo: Renga Itsuzaki’s road band lives on intimidation, stolen goods and opportunistic tolls. Its members can be funny, loyal, frightened or cruel; a joke does not make their victims’ losses harmless.
Broken Kite Band.hiddenInfo: Use the actual members, remit, resources and unresolved disputes. Rank is not omniscience; ordinary cooperation does not recruit a person or bind the player to a faction.
